formative_worksheets.title: The Same Core Check
formative_worksheets.when_to_use: After Lesson 3, before Lesson 4. Quick mid-unit check (10 minutes) to confirm A7.2 (core identification) and A7.3 (multi-representation) have landed before extending into A7.4 territory.
formative_worksheets.purpose: Standalone formative assessment distinct from lesson worksheets. Lets the teacher quickly see which children are confident with the abstract core / multi-rep concept and which need a bridging conversation before Lesson 4.
formative_worksheets.student_learning_goal: I can find the core and show it in different ways.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can find the core and show it in different ways.
header.character_watermark: Coco the Conductor in the top-right corner with a small magnifying glass — the 'check-in' Coco. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

prompts.prompt: Two of these parades have the SAME core. Circle the two parades that match.
prompts.visual_layout: Three small horizontal parade strips stacked vertically, each labelled 'Parade A', 'Parade B', 'Parade C' to the left. Each strip is 4–6 cells wide. The student draws a circle around two of the three labels (or around two of the three full strips).

image_placeholders.description: A 6-cell horizontal parade strip in B&W line-art. Cells filled in order: Bea, Finn, Bea, Finn, Bea, Finn (animal AB pattern). Footprints beneath. Label 'Parade A' to the left. Approximately 5in wide.

A 6-cell horizontal parade strip in matching style. Cells filled in order: clap, stomp, clap, stomp, clap, stomp (sound AB pattern using clap and stomp icons). Label 'Parade B' to the left. Approximately 5in wide.
A 6-cell horizontal parade strip in matching style. Cells filled in order: Bea, Finn, Finn, Bea, Finn, Finn (animal ABB pattern). Label 'Parade C' to the left. Approximately 5in wide.

prompts.answer_key: Parades A and B (both AB cores: Bea-Finn structurally equals clap-stomp). Parade C is ABB and does not match. A child who circles A+B has crossed the abstraction threshold of A7.3 — they see structure past surface.

prompts.prompt: Look at the parade at the top. Now show the SAME core a different way. Pick sounds OR bodies.
prompts.visual_layout: At the top, a pre-filled animal AB parade (6 cells). Below it, an empty 6-cell parade strip with dashed cell outlines for the student to fill. To the right of the empty strip, a small reference key showing clap, stomp, tall, and small icons.

image_placeholders.description: A 6-cell horizontal parade strip pre-filled in order: Bea, Finn, Bea, Finn, Bea, Finn (animal AB). Footprints beneath. Label 'Look at this parade:' above the strip. Full width.
An empty 6-cell horizontal parade strip with dashed cell outlines. Footprints beneath. Label 'Now show the same core another way:' above. Full width.

A small horizontal reference key with four icons: clap (open hand), stomp (footprint), tall (stick figure standing), small (stick figure crouching). Names beneath each. Each ~0.8in tall. B&W line art.

prompts.answer_key: Any valid AB pattern using a non-animal pair: clap-stomp-clap-stomp-clap-stomp; tall-small-tall-small-tall-small; hum-tap-hum-tap-hum-tap; jump-freeze-jump-freeze-jump-freeze; etc. Correct if the structural AB core is preserved AND the surface elements differ from animals.

prompts.prompt: How are you feeling about cores and same-cores-different-ways? Circle the face that fits.
prompts.visual_layout: Three faces in a horizontal row: a big smile, a neutral mouth, and a worried frown. Below each face, a label: 'I got it!', 'Almost!', 'Need help!'. The student circles one face.

image_placeholders.description: Three round face icons in a horizontal row, each ~1.5in across. Left face: B&W line-art smiling face with curved upturned mouth. Middle face: neutral straight-line mouth. Right face: line-art with downturned mouth. Below each face, printed label: 'I got it!', 'Almost!', 'Need help!'. Total row width ~6in.

prompts.answer_key: Open. The teacher uses this self-rating alongside the work on Prompts 1 and 2 to identify mismatches: a child who got Prompt 1 wrong but circled 'I got it!' may need more discussion; a child who got Prompts 1 and 2 right but circled 'Need help!' may just need confidence-building.

formative_worksheets.teacher_notes: Administer this between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4. Print one per child; circulate while children work and note who finishes confidently versus who hesitates. Score guide: 2/2 + confident self-rating = ready for Lesson 4. 2/2 + low self-rating = nudge confidence. 1/2 = brief 1:1 conference before Lesson 4 reviewing the ABB vs AB difference. 0/2 = small-group re-loop on Lesson 3's core-identification routine before continuing.

reflection_sheet.title: My Pattern Parade Reflection
reflection_sheet.purpose: End-of-unit metacognition. Children look back at their week of pattern work and rate themselves, name a favourite, name a struggle, and set a forward goal. Companion to the Lesson 5 summative — captures voice, not skill.
reflection_sheet.student_learning_goal: I can think about what I learned this week.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can think about what I learned this week.
header.character_watermark: Coco the Conductor in the top-right corner, holding a Junior Pattern Conductor certificate. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

prompts.prompt: How do you feel about being a Pattern Conductor? Circle one.
prompts.visual_layout: Three star-rating options shown horizontally, each in its own oval: 1 star, 2 stars, 3 stars. Beneath each oval, a label: 'Just starting', 'Mostly got it', 'I am a Conductor!'. Child circles one oval.

image_placeholders.description: Three options shown horizontally in ovals: left option = 1 large star (~1in), middle = 2 stars side by side, right = 3 stars side by side. Each option enclosed in a thin oval ~2in wide × 1.5in tall. Beneath each oval, printed label: 'Just starting', 'Mostly got it', 'I am a Conductor!'. Total row ~6.5in wide. B&W line art only.

prompts.prompt: Did you do these things? Circle YES or NO.
prompts.visual_layout: A four-row table. Each row contains a question label on the left and YES / NO bubbles on the right. Questions: 'I made my own parade.', 'I found the core.', 'I showed my core another way.', 'I fixed a missing animal.'.

image_placeholders.description: A bordered four-row table. Each row ~1in tall. Left column ~4in wide with question text in K-readable type. Right column ~2in wide containing two bubbles labelled 'YES' and 'NO' side by side. Total table ~6in wide. Thin grey row dividers. B&W line art only.

options: I showed my core another way.

Below the bottom-right corner, faint guide-lines for writing if the child prefers words to a drawing.

reflection_sheet.teacher_notes: Hand out at the very end of Lesson 5, alongside the Junior Pattern Conductor certificate ceremony. Children may need scribe support for prompts 3–5 — accept a drawing as a complete answer. Read responses to inform your unit notes for next year (which prompts kept emerging as 'trickiest', which moments children loved). The yes/no audit on Prompt 2 is also a quick teacher check: a 'NO' on any item signals the child either missed a key activity or doesn't recognize that they did it — worth a 30-second conference.
